subject: Post-demo recaps: Clearview deployment bridge & model routing

Subject: Post-demo recaps: Clearview deployment bridge & model routing

Thanks again for your time today, Priya & Amit — good call.  Quick recap and proposed bridge plan so we can move toward a POC environment: 

Summary of what we heard
- Primary goal: add an LLM-powered relevance/reranking layer for internal docs search and one-click summaries for analysts.
- Non-functional: <100ms median tail for search assist; cost target to be below $0.002/token on steady-state; data residency in us-east for PHI-adjacent metadata.

High-level recommended approach (starter POC)
1) Retrieval + embeddings -> candidate set (Clearview-managed vector DB)
2) Lightweight reranker on Redwood (small, low-latency model) to re-score and produce structured output (JSON schema)
3) Model routing policy: latency-first for interactive flows (route to "redwood-lowlatency-1"), cost-fallback to "redwood-medium-quant" when under heavy load, and a final safe-fallback to a deterministic template if quota exhausted.
4) Region routing: prefer us-east for the initial rollout; allow eu/apac fallbacks later.

Integration notes we should align on
- SDK: we propose Redwood SDK for request batching/streaming + structured output support. Quickstart attached.
- Auth: service-account token with KMS-wrapped keys (we'll support OAuth 2.0 client-credentials if you need OIDC integration).
- Tool-calling: use structured output with explicit function signatures to extract table rows and actionables; avoid ad-hoc parsing for POC.
- Embeddings vs reranker: embeddings for retrieval; reranker to run on short context and return score + JSON fields.

Next steps / asks
- We can provision a sandbox (us-east) if you confirm a single POC email and the initial SSO/auth approach by EOD Wed (2027-04-14).
- Request: list of 2 engineers (names + emails) who will join a 60-min architecture session next week.
- I'll assign Dev as SE owner and Lauren as engagement owner — they will follow up with a technical checklist and procurement template.

Attachments: redwood_sdk_quickstart.pdf (SDK quickstart), sample_routing_matrix.csv (attached inline as a stub)

Thanks,
Jonas Weber

Hi Priya — quick technical follow-up on the questions above (putting concrete options so your infra folks can review):

Auth options (supported today)
- Service account + API key: short-lived tokens (recommended TTL 1h) issued by Redwood; customer-managed keys via KMS can wrap the service credentials. Rotation: automatic key-rotation endpoint + webhook to notify your key manager.
- OAuth 2.0 client credentials: standard token endpoint, supports JWKS + RS256; good if you want SSO-style client identity.

Sandbox capacity
- Default sandbox: 4 vGPU serving nodes, 25 qps burst capacity, configured batching for interactive flows. We can scale to 10 vGPUs on request (turn-up time ~48 hrs). We'll instrument percentiles (p50/p90/p99) and give dashboards.

Reranker input
- Typical pattern we recommend: retrieval -> top-N raw texts + vector distances -> reranker receives (text_clip, metadata, embeddings_optional). For tight latency, pass only candidate text+metadata and let reranker compute an embedding internally if needed. Passing embeddings helps when you have a custom vector DB scoring pre-filter.

Model routing snippet (example policy)
- priority: [latency-route, cost-fallback, safe-fallback]
- latency-route: route to redwood-lowlatency-1 if estimated_token_latency < 40ms
- cost-fallback: route to redwood-medium-quant when average_cost_per_token > threshold
- safe-fallback: template-responder (deterministic) when quota_exceeded

KV cache & batching notes
- Use SDK to enable per-session KV cache for chat-style workflows and continuous batching for short-context reranking calls. This will reduce token cost and p50 latency.

I'll bring two sample configs to the architecture session and a lightweight load test plan if you want us to run an initial 10 qps test against the sandbox.

- Dev
